title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with synthetic media, a deepfake video call in which the caller presented himself as a sitting chief minister. The failure sits at the point of contact between a citizen and a consumer messaging app, not inside any institution's own system. The platform carried the call as an ordinary peer to peer video session, and nothing in that channel tied the face on screen to the office it claimed.

Catching it would have required a check the call itself could not supply. A video call offers no proof of the caller's identity, so the only reliable test was confirmation through a separate, official channel that the office had made no such offer and authorised no such intermediary. The escalating demands, each framed as a fee or a fine that had to be paid before a larger sum could be released, are the shape of an advance fee fraud rather than a failure of any automated decision.

What is not established is who made the call, whether the deepfake was produced by the same people who collected the money, and whether anyone will be convicted. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act, which is an allegation and not a finding.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A Bengaluru security guard aged 29, Ratikanta Giri, lost more than Rs 1.04 lakh after a WhatsApp video call used an AI deepfake to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller promised Rs 11 lakh in aid and said a manager would handle the transfer. The fraudsters first asked for Rs 5,000 as exchange charges, then Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN. A person claiming to be from the CBI later demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine.

Giri paid through a digital payment app. When the fraudsters asked for another Rs 50,000, he refused and realized he had been cheated. He contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then Byappanahalli police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act. This was the first such case reported in the city. Police urged people not to trust such calls or make payments based on them.
